name: Meta
level_label: Core, product sense and modeling are in the loop
summary: Primary track. Your notes have 14 dated write-ups of this loop: a recruiter, a SQL-plus-Python phone screen, then an onsite that usually includes SQL/ETL, data modeling, product sense, and ownership. Reports do not all match. The Oct 7 2026 snapshot did not find an open Toronto DE req. These prompts are from your notes. They are not sourced asked-at counts. The sourced report file has no Meta timeline.
loop: Phone screen in the notes: about 60 minutes, SQL and Python. Bookstore schema, percentages, windows, NULL, lists, and dicts.
Onsite shape that recurs: SQL/ETL, a relational model, product sense on some reports, and an ownership conversation.
One Jun 3 note adds a real-time pipeline design. One Aug 26 note says window functions were disallowed. Do not flatten those into every loop.
Oct 7 2026 snapshot: no open Toronto DE req found. That is a volume note. It does not change the study order.

rounds.name: Recruiter
rounds.focus: Several 2025 notes start here: background, past projects, and fit. One Oct 22 note puts this at about 20–30 minutes. No technical prompt list is written down.

rounds.name: Phone, SQL half
rounds.focus: The repeated phone shape is about 60 minutes split with Python. Reports mention about five SQL questions, or about 25 minutes of SQL. A bookstore schema (books, copies, authors, customers, payments) shows up more than once. Skills named: joins, aggregations, percentages, subqueries, NULL, and windows. One Aug 26 note says a medium problem where window functions were not allowed. That is one write-up, not every screen.

rounds.name: Phone, Python half
rounds.focus: The notes describe lists, dicts, strings, and sometimes a class. The named prompts are deduped in the practice bank. One Oct 22 note also includes binary search and the average length of lists. Binary search in the bank is a sourced Databricks item. This round only notes that one Meta write-up mentioned it.

rounds.name: Onsite SQL / ETL
rounds.focus: Onsited write-ups often describe one or two SQL/ETL rounds: optimizing queries, transforming raw data, and designing a pipeline. A Jun 3 note asks for a pipeline for real-time data from multiple sources, with integrity and fault tolerance. Do not treat that single prompt as the standard onsite.

rounds.name: Onsite modeling
rounds.focus: Notes describe designing a relational schema and talking through trade-offs. One Oct 22 report says the product was classroom-style and does not list tables, so there is no canonical schema to memorize. The linked models are drills from other loops, not Meta asked-at items.

rounds.name: Product sense
rounds.focus: Not in every report. A Sep 30 note describes defining metrics, with retention for a game as the example. An Oct 22 note says product sense was checked lightly. A London May 16 note lists product sense as its own interview. The practice items are drills, not reported Meta questions.

rounds.name: Ownership
rounds.focus: Notes mention collaboration, stakeholders, past challenges, and ownership. Speak from private notes. This site stores no sample story.

name: Amazon
summary: Second track, and still a timed benchmark. The July 2024 notes map six rounds, including a leadership-principles round. Use STAR templates only. Write stories locally. Oct 7 2026 snapshot: one Toronto early-career DE posting and two BIE roles. Sourced reports are the timeline below and are the only Amazon asked-at counts.
loop: Oct 7 2026 posting signals for the Toronto early-career DE role: SQL, ETL, relational versus dimensional modeling, Spark or Hadoop preferred.
July 2024 notes, phone: windows, CTE, subquery, a file word-count, and a fact/dimension sketch.
Notes, round 2: normalization, indexes, query cost, scalable ETL, most frequent element.
Notes, round 3: e-commerce model, revenue SQL, 1NF–3NF, many-to-many.
Notes, leadership round: the principles and prompts listed in the round below. No sample stories.
Notes, later technical: cleaning data, short Python drills, ETL versus ELT.
Notes, hiring manager: project depth. Placeholder only.

rounds.name: Phone screen
rounds.focus: July 2024 notes: a window, a CTE, and a subquery, plus a Python file task and a fact/dimension sketch.

rounds.name: Databases, query cost, ETL
rounds.focus: July 2024 notes: normalization versus denormalization, indexes, optimizing a large query, and an ETL for files landing in object storage. A short Python frequency task is also listed.

rounds.name: Modeling and SQL on your schema
rounds.focus: July 2024 notes: customer, product, order, order item, shipment, and payment. Then revenue per product, 1NF–3NF, when to denormalize, and many-to-many.

rounds.name: Leadership principles
rounds.focus: July 2024 notes name customer obsession, ownership, invent and simplify, deliver results, and hire and develop the best. Prompts listed there: disagreement, learning quickly, a simple solution, a tight deadline, and helping someone grow. Use STAR. Write the stories locally. Nothing on this page is a sample answer.

rounds.name: Harder SQL, Python, ETL versus ELT
rounds.focus: July 2024 notes: clean inconsistent or missing values, revenue with a join, even-number sum, a character-frequency map, and when to pick ETL or ELT. Integrity tests are a discussion, not a worksheet.

rounds.name: Hiring manager
rounds.focus: July 2024 notes: a hard project, what you would redesign, and a process you improved. Placeholder only. Do not type the story into the site.
